subject.title: [Feature]: Requester-scoped MCP connections — resolve MCP server transport per trusted sender

question: Should OpenClaw support per-requester MCP credentials inside a shared conversation session, isolating attached MCP tools by trusted sender while retaining a transcript shared by all senders in that session?
rationale: The missing requester dimension is source-supported, but the permanent plugin SDK contract and the distinction between tool authorization and transcript visibility are product and security decisions that automation cannot safely choose.

options.title: Approve requester-scoped MCP
options.body: Design one generic resolver with requester-keyed runtime ownership, credential redaction, and fail-closed behavior when trusted requester context is unavailable.

options.title: Require sender-isolated sessions
options.body: Permit per-user MCP credentials only when the conversation session and transcript are also isolated by sender, trading group-thread continuity for a stronger boundary.

options.title: Keep MCP operator-scoped
options.body: Retain static MCP transports and direct provider plugins to implement requester-aware REST tools through existing tool context.

recommendation.title: Approve requester-scoped MCP
recommendation.body: Design one generic resolver with requester-keyed runtime ownership, credential redaction, and fail-closed behavior when trusted requester context is unavailable.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work owns the central MCP runtime, transport, and cache lifecycle that would need to enforce this decision.
